memos.headline: JPM and AMZN Lead on Relative Strength; CAT and PG in Technical Trouble
memos.body: I see a clear divergence across the universe today. JPM stands out as the cleanest chart: just 1.5% off its 52-week high, +12.8% above the 200d mean, RSI at a healthy 60.4, and strong relative strength vs SPY on both 4w (+4.9%) and 12w (+10.5%) timeframes with low volatility (ATR 2.33%). AMZN is similarly strong at only 1.2% off its high with RSI 67.9, though the +10.1% extension above the 50d mean after a +17% weekly surge raises near-term mean-reversion risk. MSFT's +21.8% weekly explosion has pushed RSI to 74.5 and the price 16.4% above the 50d mean—this is a classic overbought extension that I'd fade rather than chase despite the impressive relative strength. On the downside, CAT is in a clear breakdown: RSI 36.2, -23.5% drawdown from highs, -11.4% below the 50d mean, and the worst relative strength in the universe at -15.7% over 4 weeks, while PG trades below both its 50d and 200d means with persistent negative relative strength.

views.note: Strongest risk-adjusted trend in the universe: near 52w highs, above both moving averages, moderate RSI, and leading relative strength; would reassess below 330 (roughly the 200d area).

Near 52w highs with strong 26w momentum (+13.6%) and positive relative strength, but the +17% weekly spike and 10% extension above 50d mean warrant a smaller position; a close below 245 would negate the thesis.

RSI 74.5 and +16.4% above the 50d mean after a parabolic weekly move make this a poor entry point despite strong relative strength; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d (~399) before getting constructive.
RSI 36.2, -23.5% drawdown, -15.7% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, and trading 11.4% below the 50d mean signals a broken trend; would reconsider only on a reclaim above 880.
Below both the 50d and 200d means with negative 26w returns (-3.8%) and persistent underperformance vs SPY; no reason to own until price reclaims the 200d area near 148.
Middling RSI at 48.3, flat relative strength, and sitting near the 50d mean—no edge either way; a break above 215 (toward the 52w high) would turn me constructive.
Sitting right at the 50d mean with RSI 43 after a sharp -7.2% weekly drop; the longer-term trend is intact (+24.5% over 26w) but near-term momentum is weak—need to see 300 hold as support.
12w relative strength of -11.5% vs SPY is the worst among mega-cap tech despite a bounce this week; sitting near the 50d mean with RSI 54, it's a show-me story until it reclaims 370.
Strong 26w return (+16.3%) and well above the 200d mean (+20.2%), but 4w relative strength has turned negative and RSI 47 suggests fading momentum; watching 400 as key support.
Strong 4w relative strength (+13.1%) but flat 12w returns and 9.3% drawdown from highs create a mixed picture; would get long on a sustained move above 160.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I am most convicted on the durability of earnings at NVDA and MSFT, and most concerned about deteriorating profitability at XOM and stagnation at UNH. NVDA's 2027Q1 quarter delivered $81.6B in revenue (+85% YoY) with a staggering 71.5% net margin and net income up 211% YoY on only $8.5B of total debt—this is the cleanest earnings power in the universe. MSFT's fiscal 2026Q4 10-K shows $90.0B revenue (+17.7% YoY) and $35.8B net income (+31.3% YoY) at a 39.7% net margin with moderate leverage of $40.3B, confirming durable operating leverage across cloud and AI segments. On the other side, XOM's Q1 net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2% with flat net income and a 5.6% margin burdened by $77.9B in debt. GOOGL's Q2 net margin of 93.7% and 298% net income growth look extraordinary and likely include a large one-time gain, so I want to see the segment detail before sizing a position; I mark it neutral pending that clarity.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, 71.5% net margin, minimal debt of $8.5B—best earnings power profile in the universe; would reassess if margins compress below 55%.
FY2026 10-K shows 39.7% net margin and 31% net income growth on 17.7% revenue growth, demonstrating durable operating leverage with manageable $40.3B debt.
93.7% net margin and 298% net income growth almost certainly include a large non-recurring item; need segment-level detail before taking a directional view.
Revenue of $181.5B (+16.6% YoY) with net income up 77% to $30.3B and margin expanding to 16.7% is encouraging, though $122.6B total debt warrants monitoring.
$111.2B revenue (+16.6% YoY) and 26.6% net margin are solid, but $82.7B debt and only 19% earnings growth lag peers; would upgrade if services mix drives margin expansion.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% YoY with a 14.6% net margin show strong cyclical momentum, but $36.2B debt and cycle-peak risk temper conviction.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33% net margin are respectable for a bank, but $448.8B total debt and only 12.6% earnings growth limit upside.
Defensive 18.5% net margin and 7.4% revenue growth are fine but unexciting; I see no catalyst for re-rating.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin signals severe cash-flow compression; would revisit only if commodity prices meaningfully recover.
Flat net income, only 2% revenue growth, 5.6% net margin, and $77.9B debt point to earnings stagnation with no margin of safety.

memos.headline: Fed Paused at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% CPI and Rising Long Yields Signal No Near-Term Easing — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months with 75 bps of cuts already delivered over the past year, yet headline CPI is running at 3.5% y/y — well above target and likely keeping the FOMC on hold through at least Q3. The 10-year yield has climbed 35 bps over three months to 4.75%, compressing equity multiples on long-duration growth names, while the 10y-2y spread has narrowed slightly to +45 bps, consistent with a late-cycle environment rather than imminent recession. The labor market is resilient at 4.2% unemployment (down 10 bps over three months), which supports consumer-facing cyclicals and bank net interest income but removes any urgency for further cuts. A CPI print falling below 3.0% y/y or unemployment breaching 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing and make me more constructive on duration-sensitive tech.

views.note: Pause regime with a positively sloped curve at +45 bps and resilient employment supports bank NII; JPM is the highest-quality way to play this.
Rising 10y yields to 4.75% pressure long-duration equity valuations, but strong consumer employment limits downside; I stay on the sideline.
Most duration-sensitive name in the universe faces headwinds from a 35 bps backup in the 10y over three months with no easing catalyst in sight.
Quality growth but still long-duration; sticky 3.5% CPI keeps the Fed on hold and the 10y elevated, capping multiple expansion.
Defensive staple with pricing power benefits from a late-cycle pause regime and resilient consumer spending at 4.2% unemployment.
Stable labor market supports demand, but no clear macro catalyst either way; energy is more an oil-price call than a rates call here.
Cyclical bellwether benefits from solid employment but faces margin pressure if the late-cycle pause extends and capex slows.
Consumer resilience is a positive, but rising long-end yields weigh on the growth multiple; net effect is roughly balanced.
Similar duration headwinds as other mega-cap tech; pause regime offers no valuation tailwind until inflation convincingly declines.
Defensive healthcare with stable demand profile suits a late-cycle pause; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Earnings Season Splits the Mega-Caps: MSFT and AMZN Surge While AAPL and GOOGL Sell Off Hard
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal this cycle. MSFT jumped +15.5% on its 7/29 results and AMZN surged +15.3% on its 7/30 print, indicating overwhelmingly positive narrative shifts that likely have further room to run as buy-side positioning catches up. Conversely, AAPL dropped -7.4% on its 7/30 report and GOOGL fell -7.1% on its 7/22 results, signaling negative sentiment pivots that may not yet be fully digested. JPM's modest +2.5% reaction on 7/14 and UNH's +1.2% on 7/16 suggest muted but constructive tone, while PG's -1.9% on 7/29 reflects mild disappointment in a defensive name. I have highest conviction on the MSFT and AMZN long calls given the magnitude of the positive reactions, and I would avoid AAPL near-term given the severity of its selloff suggests a genuine narrative deterioration rather than noise.

views.note: A +15.5% post-earnings move signals a major positive sentiment shift that likely attracts further momentum flows.
The +15.3% earnings-day surge is the strongest positive reaction in the universe and suggests a durable narrative upgrade.
A -7.4% post-earnings drop on 7/30-31 points to a sharp negative sentiment turn that likely has not fully priced through yet.
The -7.1% selloff on 7/22-23 earnings plus multiple board-level changes earlier in the quarter create an unsettled narrative.
A +2.5% post-earnings reaction is constructive but modest; steady filing cadence suggests no negative surprises ahead.
The +1.2% earnings reaction is tepid and I lack enough tone data to form a strong directional view.
A -1.9% earnings reaction is mild for a defensive staple; sentiment is slightly negative but not alarming.
No earnings reaction data available this cycle; recent filings are routine governance items with no clear sentiment signal.
The 7/1 acquisition-related 8-K is complex but no earnings reaction is available to gauge market sentiment.
Only a routine shareholder vote and Reg FD filing; insufficient data to take a directional sentiment view.

memos.headline: Oil Spike and Elevated Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Supply-Side Stress; NVDA and XOM Most Exposed
memos.body: I see a mixed but watchable geopolitical backdrop as of today. WTI crude surged 20.7% over the past month to $85.15/bbl, even as it remains down 21.6% over three months—this kind of sharp one-month reversal typically reflects a supply disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than demand strength, and I treat it as a potential structural shift until proven otherwise. The Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 338, still elevated historically despite a 12.5% decline over three months, while VIX at 17.09 has crept up nearly 4% in the last month—consistent with markets beginning to price incremental geopolitical risk. HY spreads at 2.84% are essentially flat over three months (+1 bp), so credit markets are not yet signaling contagion, which limits my conviction on a broad risk-off call. My key concern is the intersection of energy security risk (benefiting XOM, pressuring cost structures for AMZN and CAT) and ongoing export-control overhang on advanced semiconductors (NVDA), where any tightening of China-facing rules would be a structural headwind; a formal easing of chip export controls or a credible OPEC+ supply increase would change my views.

views.note: Export-control risk to China revenue remains the dominant geopolitical overhang; no evidence of policy easing, but no new restrictions either, so I stay neutral rather than avoid.
The 20.7% one-month WTI spike to $85.15 likely reflects supply-side geopolitical tightening, which structurally benefits XOM's upstream margins.
Higher energy costs pressure logistics margins, but AMZN's diversified model and two recent 8-K filings suggest ongoing corporate activity that may offset; low conviction either way.
CAT benefits from infrastructure spending but faces input-cost pressure from the oil spike and elevated policy uncertainty; Reg FD disclosure in June adds no clarity on geopolitical positioning.
Defensive consumer staples tend to outperform when policy uncertainty is elevated at 338; multiple recent Reg FD filings suggest active investor communication, which I read as management confidence.
Steepening yield curve (+15 bp in one month) is a tailwind for bank NII, but elevated policy uncertainty and four 8-K filings in five weeks suggest a complex regulatory or capital-action environment.

Hold ~30% cash given elevated rates, sticky inflation, and overbought conditions in several names.
